facts.fact: Oeil d'Afrique reports that RDC-PASS, a digital identifier meant to provide biometric authentication for SIM registration, unified access to administrative platforms and automated customer identity checks, was activated on 13 June 2026 under a 20-year public-private partnership, with 50 enrolment agents trained on 15 September 2026 and a pilot phase in Kinshasa to follow.

COD.note: The document says nothing on records passing between the civil register and RDC-PASS.
Enrolment has only begun with a first cohort of agents; no count or share of people enrolled is given.
The document says nothing on an identity number given at birth.

The operator is the Congolese subsidiary of a Singapore-based company under a 20-year partnership, but the document says hosting and data ownership are not public and does not say who runs or maintains the system day to day.
No public register keyed on the identifier is named.

facts.fact: Oeil d'Afrique reports that RDC-PASS, which the government says is not a national identity card but an access key backed by a biometric database, is to be attributed to every Congolese by 2030, with enrolment agents trained on 15 September 2026 and a Kinshasa pilot to follow.
